official_measurement_examples.name: Second-stair commencement
official_measurement_examples.fact: Approved Document B amendments introducing a second-stair threshold for blocks of flats with a storey 18 metres or more are scheduled to take effect on 30 September 2026, subject to transitional arrangements.

official_measurement_examples.name: Transition period
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 2026 second-stair amendments preserve earlier guidance for qualifying applications where work is sufficiently progressed within the stated 18-month transition framework.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 consultation status
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Building Safety Regulator consultation on further Approved Document B changes ran from 25 March to 1 July 2026 and is a closed consultation, not adopted guidance.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2029 target
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 2026 consultation targets 2 September 2029 for the proposed further guidance changes, subject to the post-consultation decision process.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning gateway one
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning gateway one requires specified fire-safety information and consultation at planning stage for relevant high-rise residential development, but does not replace Building Regulations approval.

official_measurement_examples.name: Fire Safety England Regulations scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Fire Safety (England) Regulations 2022 impose operational duties on responsible persons in multi-occupied residential buildings, including additional duties for taller buildings.

official_measurement_examples.name: High-rise accountable-person regime
official_measurement_examples.fact: Building Safety Regulator guidance describes high-rise residential buildings in the occupied regime as at least 18 metres or 7 storeys with at least 2 residential units.

official_measurement_examples.name: Approved Document role
official_measurement_examples.fact: Approved Document B provides statutory guidance on ways to meet Part B Building Regulations requirements; following it is not planning permission and does not itself determine every unusual case.
